answer: A place I really enjoy shopping is Jamuna Future Park, a huge, modern shopping mall in Dhaka, which I usually visit when I am staying with my elder sister. It is one of the biggest shopping centres in the country, so you could easily spend a whole day there. I mostly buy clothes, especially new shirts and a panjabi before Eid, and sometimes books or small gifts for my younger sister. I go there perhaps every two or three months, depending on how often I travel to Dhaka. What I like about it is that everything is [[under one roof]], which makes it wonderfully [[convenient]]. It has [[a vast array of]] shops, from local brands to international ones, so I can compare prices without walking from market to market in the heat. Beyond the shopping itself, it is a pleasant place to spend a few hours; it is clean, air-conditioned and has good places to eat. I often go with my sister and her husband, and my nephew loves the play area, so it doubles as a family outing. What makes it enjoyable is the lively but comfortable atmosphere, which is never too [[overwhelming]], except perhaps in the last few days before Eid. Honestly, even when I do not buy much, I enjoy just browsing and [[window-shopping]]. I think a good shopping centre is designed to be an experience, not just a transaction, and this one gets that balance right. Back home, I still prefer local shops for everyday things, but for special purchases this is my favourite place.

followUps.q: Do you prefer shopping in malls or in local markets?
followUps.answer: For clothes and special purchases, I prefer malls because of the choice and fixed prices. For everyday things like fruit and vegetables, I always go to the local market, where everything is fresher and cheaper.
Yes, more and more, mainly for books and small electronics. It is convenient, but I still like to see and touch clothes before buying them, so for those I usually go to a shop.

note: Sirajganj has no big mall, so set in Dhaka (Jamuna Future Park) on visits to his sister, frequency adjusted; added what he buys (Eid panjabi); plain marks 'choice' and 'pleasant' replaced by 'a vast array of' and 'window-shopping', added 'under one roof'.
